relations.note: Written to obey 'Euer Königlichen Majestät allerhöchstem Befehl vom 18 November ... nach welchem der Titulus possessionis über die Hochfürstlich Hohenlohischen Güter Kopojno, Zagórów, Drzewce, p. p. berichtiget werden soll'. Document 30 is that order, of 18 November 1800, over the same estates. Note that 29 is subscribed 'Breslau den 3ten Novbr 1800', which is BEFORE the order it answers: ruled by the editor, 2026-09-17, an error in the original document rather than a misreading, so the link stands and the date is left as written.

text:
Copia
Allerdurchlauchtigster Großmächtigster König!
allergnädigster König und Herr!
Euer Königlichen Majestät allerhöchstem Befehl vom 18
November allerunterthänigst zu folgen, nach welchem der
Titulus possessionis über die Hochfürstlich Hohenlohischen
Güter Kopojno, Zagorowo, Drzewce, p. p. berichtiget
werden soll, habe ich für die Beybringung derer Do¬
kumente alles erforderliche gethan, und ich hoffe daß
der bißher obgewaltete Anstand gehoben, und Euer Maje¬
stäts allerhöchsten Befehle binnen 4 Wochen genauest voll¬
zogen werden können, daher, alle ernstliche Verfügungen
hiergegen aufzuhalten, ich allerunterthänigst bitte, der ich
in tiefster Ehrfurcht ersterbe
Euer Königlichen Majestät
allerunterthänigster
Johann Wilhelm Glenck
fürstl. Hohenlohischen Bau u Oeconomi
Rath.
Breslau den 3ten Novbr
1800

translation.en:
Copy

Most Serene and Most Mighty King! Most gracious King and Lord!

In most humble obedience to Your Royal Majesty's most high command of 18 November, according to which the title of possession (titulus possessionis) to the Princely Hohenlohe estates of Kopojno, Zagórów, Drzewce, etc. etc. is to be rectified, I have done everything required for the production of the documents, and I hope that the impediment which has hitherto prevailed is removed, and that Your Majesty's most high commands may be most exactly carried out within 4 weeks; wherefore I most humbly beg that all severe measures against this be held back, and in deepest reverence I remain, until death, Your Royal Majesty's most humble Johann Wilhelm Glenck, Princely Hohenlohe Councillor of Building and Economy.

Wrocław, the 3rd of November 1800

text_english:
Copy

Most Serene and Most Mighty King! Most gracious King and Lord!

In most humble obedience to Your Royal Majesty's most high command of 18 November, according to which the title of possession (titulus possessionis) to the Princely Hohenlohe estates of Kopojno, Zagórów, Drzewce, etc. etc. is to be rectified, I have done everything required for the production of the documents, and I hope that the impediment which has hitherto prevailed is removed, and that Your Majesty's most high commands may be most exactly carried out within 4 weeks; wherefore I most humbly beg that all severe measures against this be held back, and in deepest reverence I remain, until death, Your Royal Majesty's most humble Johann Wilhelm Glenck, Princely Hohenlohe Councillor of Building and Economy.

Wrocław, the 3rd of November 1800
summary_en: A copy of a letter of Johann Wilhelm Glenck, the Prince of Hohenlohe's councillor for building and estate management, to the King: in obedience to the King's order to put in order the title to the Prince's estates of Kopojno, Zagórów, Drzewce and others, he has done everything needed to supply the documents. He hopes that the obstacle so far is removed and the order can be carried out within four weeks, and asks that all severe measures be held off. The order he answers is dated 18 November, his letter 3 November.
summary_de: Abschrift eines Schreibens Johann Wilhelm Glencks, des Bau- und Ökonomierats des Fürsten zu Hohenlohe, an den König: Dem königlichen Befehl gemäß, den Besitztitel der fürstlichen Güter Kopojno, Zagórów, Drzewce und anderer zu berichtigen, habe er alles getan, um die Urkunden beizubringen. Er hofft, das bisherige Hindernis sei behoben und der Befehl könne binnen vier Wochen ausgeführt werden, und bittet, alle strengen Verfügungen aufzuschieben. Der Befehl, auf den er antwortet, ist auf den 18. November datiert, sein Schreiben auf den 3. November.
